title: First Steps of the BRIDGE-AI Mushroom Pilot in Kenya
audience: Farmers, students, researchers, agricultural practitioners, technology developers, project partners, and local communities
location: Smart Mushroom Farm, Jomo Kenyatta University of Agriculture and Technology (JKUAT), Kenya
summary: The BRIDGE-AI Smart Mushroom pilot is taking shape in Kenya, with students, researchers, and technical teams working at JKUAT's Smart Mushroom Farm on environmental monitoring, IoT sensors, digital dashboards, and data collection systems.
body:
The first steps of the BRIDGE-AI Smart Mushroom pilot are underway in Kenya at the Smart Mushroom Farm hosted by Jomo Kenyatta University of Agriculture and Technology (JKUAT).

Students, researchers, and technical teams are working together to establish key components of the pilot, including environmental monitoring systems, IoT sensors, digital dashboards, and data collection infrastructure. These building blocks will form part of an integrated ecosystem for more sustainable and data-driven mushroom farming.

The pilot will investigate how sensor data and local environmental conditions can be combined with Generative AI to provide practical recommendations for farmers. By using data collected from the mushroom growing environment, the project aims to support better decision-making and help farmers optimise growing conditions.

The BRIDGE-AI approach will also explore opportunities to improve resource efficiency and strengthen the resilience of agricultural production in the face of climate-related challenges.

The activity represents an important early milestone in the implementation of the Kenyan pilot and brings together technical expertise, research, student participation, and agricultural innovation.

BRIDGE-AI acknowledges the contribution of Jomo Kenyatta University of Agriculture and Technology (JKUAT), JHUB Africa, and all students, researchers, technical teams, and partners involved in advancing the Smart Mushroom pilot in Kenya.

title: JAMBO101 & MAMBO101: JHUB Africa Showcases the Future of Smart Mushroom Farming
location: JKUAT Smart Farm Zone, Juja, Kenya
summary: JHUB Africa, through Jomo Kenyatta University of Agriculture and Technology (JKUAT), in partnership with Mush& and the KOICA CTS Program, officially launched the JAMBO101 and MAMBO101 mushroom strains and unveiled the Smart Mushroom Farm at Technology House, JKUAT, on 18 August 2026.
body:
On 18th August 2026, Jomo Kenyatta University of Agriculture and Technology (JKUAT), through JHUB Africa, in partnership with Mush& and the KOICA CTS Program, hosted the official launch of the JAMBO101 and MAMBO101 mushroom strains and the unveiling of the Smart Mushroom Farm at Technology House, JKUAT.

The showcase brought together JKUAT institutional leadership, researchers, staff and students, alongside representatives from KOICA Kenya, Mush&, and the wider innovation and climate-smart agriculture ecosystem.

Among those present were Prof. George Thiong’o, Principal, COPAS; Dr. Patrick Mbindyo, Registrar, RPE; Wankyu Park, Country Director, KOICA Kenya Office; Jihyun Jung, CEO, Mush&; and innovation leaders from JHUB Africa.

Opening the session, Dr. Lawrence Nderu, Founder and Director of JHUB Africa, highlighted the importance of creating practical spaces where research, technology and entrepreneurship can come together to address real agricultural challenges.

Speaking on the biotechnology behind the launch, Jihyun Jung, CEO of Mush&, highlighted that the JAMBO101 and MAMBO101 strains were developed for local climate conditions and high yields, helping smallholder farmers increase income through small-scale production.

Prof. George Thiong’o, Principal of COPAS, highlighted the potential of computing technology and AI to address real-world challenges across the Sustainable Development Goals.

Dr. Patrick Mbindyo, Registrar, RPE, added that facilities such as the Smart Mushroom Farm bridge academic research and practical application, enabling hands-on learning and viable student-led ventures.

Wankyu Park, Country Director of the KOICA Kenya Office, described the launch as a significant scientific achievement, noting that the new mushroom strains and Smart Mushroom Farm provide a controlled environment for climate-smart testing.

The launch demonstrated how university research, biotechnology, IoT-enabled agriculture, artificial intelligence and entrepreneurship can converge to support practical agricultural innovation.

In the closing remarks, the partners reaffirmed the importance of continued collaboration in developing solutions that strengthen food systems, create opportunities for young innovators and advance climate-smart agriculture.

title: Bridging Research and Market Impact: How Strategic Ecosystems Drive Sustainable Agricultural Innovation
location: JKUAT Smart Farm Zone, Juja, Kenya
summary: The launch of the JAMBO101 and MAMBO101 mushroom strains and unveiling of the Smart Mushroom Farm at JKUAT highlighted how strategic innovation ecosystems can help move agricultural research beyond university laboratories and toward practical, climate-resilient community impact.
body:
The launch of the JAMBO101 and MAMBO101 mushroom strains and the unveiling of the Smart Mushroom Farm on 18th August 2026 at Tech House, Jomo Kenyatta University of Agriculture and Technology (JKUAT), raised an important question: how can agricultural research move beyond university laboratories and contribute to practical, climate-resilient community impact?

At JHUB Africa, our role as a digital innovation hub is to support sustainable digital transformation by developing accessible and impactful solutions for small- and medium-scale farmers.

One important lesson is that innovation becomes more valuable when it moves beyond the laboratory. Research can generate new knowledge, but smart farms and living innovation environments create opportunities to test, learn and improve those ideas under practical conditions.

The Smart Mushroom Farm therefore represents more than a structure for mushroom production. It creates a practical environment where students and researchers can interact with technology, observe agricultural processes and explore how emerging solutions can respond to changing production conditions.

Such environments provide opportunities for hands-on learning, experimentation and collaboration between academia, technology developers, farmers and industry partners.

The broader opportunity is to build smarter farms while developing a generation of innovators who understand how technology can be applied to real agricultural challenges. By connecting research, practical experimentation and entrepreneurship, innovation ecosystems can help transform agricultural knowledge into solutions with wider social and economic impact.

The Smart Mushroom Farm provides a practical foundation for this approach, demonstrating how research institutions and innovation hubs can work together to create environments where agricultural technology can be tested, refined and shared.
